titulo: Om Mani Padme Hum x5: Cleanse Your Karma (or Just Lower Your Cortisol)
caption:
Om Mani Padme Hum x5: Cleanse Your Karma (or Just Lower Your Cortisol)

Oṃ Maṇi Padme Hūṃ, said the Tibetan way: Om Mani Peme Hung.

What it is: the six-syllable mantra of Avalokiteśvara (Chenrezig in Tibetan), the bodhisattva of compassion, recited, carved and spun in prayer wheels across Tibetan Buddhism. Mani means jewel and padme lotus; the Dalai Lama explains the jewel as compassion and the lotus as wisdom. The Sanskrit is Om Mani Padme Hum; Tibetans say "peme" and "hung", and that's how it's chanted here.

In the tradition: it is chanted to call up Chenrezig's compassion for all beings. The Dalai Lama teaches that the six syllables stand for a path that unites method and wisdom, which can turn an impure body, speech and mind into those of a Buddha.

Why a sound like this can calm you: in a 2001 BMJ study, 23 healthy adults recited "om-mani-padme-om" and the rosary; both slowed breathing to about 6 breaths a minute and made the heart-rhythm reflexes stronger (Bernardi et al.). In a 2024 study, 34 adults chanted "om" for 12 minutes and their saliva cortisol and anxiety went down (Perry, Polito & Thompson); there was no group that didn't chant. In a pilot brain scan of 12 people, chanting "om" lowered activity in emotion areas, the amygdala among them, compared with rest; saying "ssss" did not (Kalyani et al., 2011). Small studies, short effects: calmer, not cured.

And if karma is real, this should clean a little of yours. Good karma, joy, or both.

Chant it five times with him. Then once more.

Sources: Bernardi et al. 2001, BMJ; Perry, Polito & Thompson 2024, J Relig Health; Kalyani et al. 2011, Int J Yoga; the Dalai Lama, On the meaning of Om Mani Padme Hum. Full references in the YouTube description.

Voice: synthetic (ElevenLabs). Drone, tanpura and bowl composed with code by NAOS. Corrections welcome.
Closer to yourself.

alt: A 16-second vertical video with a deep man's synthetic voice chanting Om Mani Peme Hung five times over a soft drone with a tanpura and a bowl. No figures: a night sky with a thin crescent moon, stars, a cloud, low hills and a dark tree; the camera zooms in slowly and comes back. White text reads OM MANI PADME HUM · CHANT ALONG, then Oṃ Maṇi Padme Hūṃ, and below it said in Tibetan: Om Mani Peme Hung. Five small beads fill with gold, one for each repetition.

-14.1 LUFS integrated, true peak -1.2 dBTP (D-346); voice in front with a short room; drone composed with code (empresa/mantras/audio16.py on motor/musica/midi.py, FluidSynth + FluidR3_GM: warm pad on Sa-Pa-Sa, tanpura pattern Pa-Sa-Sa-Sa on the GM sitar, a soft bowl in and out; Sa = G#, the most frequent pitch of the voice), about 11 dB under the voice, no percussion, no third-party recordings

mantra in IAST transliteration, 84 to 96 px, between y 935 and 1300 (the bottom free for Shorts and Reels UI), white with a soft shadow; the line or bead being sung lights up from the ElevenLabs alignment (empresa/mantras/texto16.py)

chanted as Tibetans say it, Om Mani Peme Hung (padme -> peme, hum -> hung: Encyclopedia of Religion entry, purifymind.com breakdown); Sanskrit IAST on screen; ElevenLabs speech-to-text heard the six syllables in each repetition
